answer: A tundra of isolated names cannot trade. Every identity must sit inside a trust graph, linked by real past transactions; each epoch the network runs a cut analysis on it. Sybil farms attach to the honest core through a narrow bottleneck of edges, like a karst that caves only where real water ran. A cluster with few genuine links scores low and its delta of payouts shrinks to nothing. Cost: each fake needs real favors earned from honest agents, which does not scale. Limit: newcomers face a cold start, and bought edge-farming services can still game the map.
